core_obligations: Recover a null sequence in the target from a rapidly decreasing source sequence using only the ternary triangle relation.
Use triangles with one small side to prove uniform continuity away from zero.
Separate the two components outside each triangle interval and recover additivity from their boundary behavior.
Use rational approximation from below and truncated-addition closure to prove a common positive scale factor, without assuming division closure of the distance set.

proof_roadmap.step: Derive density and a rapidly decreasing image null sequence, then continuity/uniform continuity away from zero.
Recover triangle-interval complements, rule out mixing their two sides by small-step chains, and identify the additive boundary.
Approximate t/x by rationals and x/m from below within the distance set; use continuity and existing finite sums to get f(t)/t=f(x)/x.

difficulty_reason: A bare triangle-preserving bijection need not be assumed monotone or continuous. The proof reconstructs these analytic constraints from the relational structure, then obtains additivity and a single scale factor even when the domain is only a countable truncated additive set and is not closed under division. The null-sequence and rational-approximation arguments solve those specific obstructions.

compared.difference: The public item assumes inf=1 and unbounded sup, and gets equality of normalized sets. Here inf=0, including bounded sets, and every triangle-isomorphism is multiplication by one positive real.
The other new task constructs nonrigid bounded sets with positive infimum that code arbitrary order isomorphism; this is the opposite accumulating-at-zero rigidity theorem.
Rado spanning-subgraph equivalence for a nontrivial neighbourhood filter; no triangle-isomorphism coding or scalar rigidity.
Back-and-forth ranks for ordinal powers of integer orders, not triangle equivalence of distance value sets.
Integral separating vector under a triangular matrix action, not coding or rigidity of metric triangles.
Two bounded-component Borel covers obtained from a forward-independent hitting set, not metric triangle equivalence.
